This file provides guidance to Coding Agent when working with code in this repository.

## What is PegaInfer

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

**Supported models:**

Every model line is behind a cargo feature; only `qwen3` is a default feature, so the stock build is pure Rust + CUDA with no Python.

| Model | Crate | Feature flag | Architecture |
|-------|-------|-------------|-------------|
| Qwen3-4B / 8B | `pegainfer-qwen3` | `qwen3` (default) | Full attention, TP support |
| Qwen3.5-4B / 9B / 27B · Qwen3.8-27B | `pegainfer-qwen35` | `--features qwen35` (needs build-time Python + Triton) | Hybrid Gated DeltaNet + full attention. Qwen3.8 shares the line: same `model_type`, same text geometry — see `docs/models/qwen35/support-qwen38.md` |
| DeepSeek-V2-Lite | `pegainfer-deepseek-v2-lite` | `--features deepseek-v2-lite` | MoE + EP, 2-GPU |
| Gemma 4 | `pegainfer-gemma4` | `--features gemma4` | Sliding-window + global full attention, dense sizes at TP2 (one rank per device), batched decode, opt-in chunked prefill (single rank only) |
| Kimi-K2 | `pegainfer-kimi-k2` | `--features kimi-k2` | MLA + MoE + Marlin INT4, 8-GPU EP |
| GLM5.2 | `pegainfer-glm52` | `--features glm52` | MLA + MoE + FP8, 8-GPU EP (bring-up) |
| Kimi-K3 | `pegainfer-k3` | `--features k3` | Hybrid KDA + MLA, latent MoE + MXFP4, EP (bring-up — single-rank decode wired) |

## Build & Run

**Always use `--release`** — debug builds are extremely slow for GPU/CUDA and will timeout.

When developing with Docker, use `docker/Dockerfile.dev` and `docker/dev.sh` as described in `docker/README.md`.

```bash
# Qwen3 (default feature, no Python anywhere in the build)
cargo run --release -- --model-path models/Qwen3-4B

# Feature-gated models
cargo run --release --features qwen35 -- --model-path models/Qwen3.5-4B
cargo run --release --features kimi-k2 -- --model-path models/Kimi-K2
cargo run --release --features deepseek-v2-lite -- --model-path models/DeepSeek-V2-Lite
cargo run --release --features glm52 -- --model-path models/GLM5.2
```

**Key env vars:**
- `PEGAINFER_CUDA_SM` — GPU SM target override when `nvidia-smi` unavailable (e.g. `120` or `120,80`)
- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)
- `PEGAINFER_TILELANG_PYTHON` — Python with TileLang for the `glm52` sparse-MLA build-time AOT (sm_90a targets only)
- `PEGAINFER_NCCL_ROOT` — NCCL root (>= 2.30.4) for DeepEP shim (`moe` feature)
- `PEGAINFER_FLASHINFER_INCLUDE` — FlashInfer include dir override
- `PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH` — override test model path (default: `models/Qwen3-4B`)
- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). Append-only text, created if absent, safe to share between processes and machines and safe to delete; each record carries GPU, CUDA runtime/driver/cublasLt version, shape and workspace cap, so anything that does not match is a miss and re-tunes (a driver update that keeps the same CUDA level is not distinguished — delete the file to force a re-tune). Unset = tune on every boot; Qwen3's `--batch-invariant` pins the heuristic instead and never reads it
- `PEGAINFER_GLOBAL_ATTN` — gemma4 global-attention kernel and pool format: unset/`off` = the incumbent kernel on the split K|V pool (byte-identical serving); `tilelang` = the generated kernel on the same pool; `tilelang640` = the generated kernel on a folded pool whose rows hold K only where the rotation touches it and fold K's norm weight into the query, 640 columns per token per head instead of 1024. Both generated states also read the sliding family's prompt rows through a generated windowed prefill and its pure-decode rows through a generated windowed split-KV kernel, project Q|K|V and gate|up with one GEMM each where the split state issues one per projection (the fused shape may round differently), need a build that carries the kernels, and report the global pool's bytes at start-up
- `PEGAINFER_KV_FP8` — gemma4 opt-in fp8 KV: `local` stores the sliding family's K/V as e4m3 at scale 1.0 (lossy; halves the local pool; refuses an enabled prefix cache; unset = byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_PREFIX_CACHE` — gemma4 opt-in conversation prefix cache: `K` entries of captured prompt state resume multi-turn prompts (pre-allocated page budget; unset = off, byte-identical serving)
- `PEGAINFER_ADMIT_COALESCE_MS` — gemma4 opt-in admission coalesce door: `N` ms in `1..=2000` (`off`/`0`/unset = admit on sight), holds arrivals that would invade a live decode batch so a window's arrivals land as one admission burst; refuses the async prefill lane; merging into one mixed step needs the chunked walk or a sub-budget prompt
- `PEGAINFER_ASYNC_PREFILL` — gemma4 opt-in overlap lane: `green:NN` prefills live-batch admissions on an SM-capped stream to protect decode tails (`shared` for comparison; unset = off; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` — gemma4 opt-in chunked walk: a mixed admission computes at most `N` prompt rows per step (`64 <= N <` the serving ceiling; unset = whole-prompt steps; bad values refuse to start)
- `PEGAINFER_MIX_GATHER_ROWS` / `PEGAINFER_MIX_MAX_PROMPTS` — gemma4 admission gather: how many prompt rows and how many prompts one mixed step may absorb (`1..=` the serving ceiling and `1..=` the decode slots; defaults gather only short bursts). Raising them lets a burst ride one step, which trades the median time to first token for the p99 tail and the wide-batch decode step; bad values refuse to start
- `PEGAINFER_MAX_CONTEXT` — gemma4 serving ceiling raise (default 8192, up to the checkpoint's 262144; a raise past the default needs `PEGAINFER_MIX_CHUNK_TOKENS` and refuses the async lane)
- `PEGAINFER_DECODE_SLOTS` — gemma4 decode slots (1..16, default 16): global KV budget = slots x ceiling, trade concurrency for context
- `GLM52_DECODE_SLOTS` / `GLM52_MTP_DRAFTS` — glm52 runtime profile: decode slots per rank (default 8, ceiling 32) and MTP draft span (default 5); `slots x (1+drafts)` must fit the 96-row step (validated at launch; MTP only). Throughput ceiling profile: `32` / `2`.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP` — k3 opt-in context-parallel prefill lane: CP width, must equal the process's local rank count (on a fleet each process runs its own gang; remote ranks pad). Mutually exclusive with the dspark draft lane.
- `PEGAINFER_K3_CP_MIN` — k3 CP admission floor in prompt tokens (default 2048; measured crossover ~1k). Prompts below it, or too long for one chunk step per rank (M0), prefill locally.

## Tests

```bash
# Unit tests (~9s)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib

# Lines gated on their own kernel feature need it named to run their unit tests.
# The K3 command also names the kernels crate, whose K3 tests ride the same
# feature:
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-k3 -p pegainfer-kernels --features k3 --lib
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-glm52 --features glm52 --lib

# Accuracy and integration tests — require GPU + model weights
cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen3 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test hf_golden_gate
PEGAINFER_TEST_MODEL_PATH=models/Qwen3.5-4B cargo test --release -p pegainfer-qwen35 --features qwen35 --test e2e_scheduler

# Single test (filter by name)
cargo test --release --workspace --lib prefix_cache -- --nocapture
```

Qwen accuracy gates compare logits against stored HF golden fixtures. Qwen3.5 exact-text JSON baselines are retired; keep `e2e_scheduler` for scheduler liveness and request-flow coverage.

## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Pure Rust + CUDA LLM inference engine. No PyTorch, no frameworks. OpenAI-compatible `/v1/completions` API.

- `PEGAINFER_TRITON_PYTHON` — Python with Triton for `qwen35` build-time AOT kernel generation (falls back to `.venv/bin/python`, then `python3`, then `python`)

- `PEGAINFER_BUILD_TIMING=1` — print per-phase build timings (nvcc, Triton AOT, etc.)
- `PEGAINFER_NVCC_JOBS` — override parallel nvcc job count
- `PEGAINFER_GEMM_LT_CACHE` — opt-in cross-process cublasLt algo store: `<file>` carries the winners `gemm_lt_tune` timed in an earlier boot instead of re-timing them (Qwen3-4B on one sm_89 card: warm ready ~1965 → ~1312 ms, paired 5/5). ## Architecture

```
HTTP Request → vLLM frontend → EngineHandle → per-model scheduler/executor → TokenEvent
                                               │
              ┌──────────┬─────────────┬───────┼───────────┬──────────┐
              │          │             │       │           │          │
        pegainfer-  pegainfer-   pegainfer-  pegainfer-  pegainfer-  ...
        qwen3       qwen35       dsv2-lite   kimi-k2     glm52
      (full attn) (linear+full) (MoE+EP)   (MLA+MoE)  (MLA+MoE+FP8)
              │          │             │       │           │          │
              └──────────┴─────────────┴───────┼───────────┴──────────┘
                                               │
                          pegainfer-core runtime + pegainfer-kernels
                                               │
                               ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                               │               │               │
                       CUDA / cuBLAS    Triton AOT      FlashInfer
                                                    (sampling, attention,
                                                     norm, MLA decode)
```

**Key abstractions:**

- **`pegainfer-frontend`** — the serving frontend: the engine request/event contract (`pegainfer_frontend::engine` — `EngineHandle`, `GenerateRequest`, `TokenEvent`) plus the protocol stacks on top of it (`vllm` module today, `dynamo` planned) and the `ModelLine` dispatch trait. Model crates implement against the contract; the server binary does pure dispatch.
- **Per-model crates** — each model owns config, weights, prefill/decode execution, scheduler, tests, and benches.
- **`pegainfer-core::ops`** — shared GPU operator wrappers used by model crates.
- **`pegainfer-kernels`** — tensor/FFI/kernel build owner for CUDA, cuBLAS, FlashInfer, and Triton AOT. Model-specific kernels live in feature-gated submodules (`kimi_k2`, `glm52`).
- **CUDA Graph** — decode path captured inside model executors with pre-allocated buffers to preserve pointer stability.
- **KV state** — model schedulers own request state; shared paged-KV primitives live in `pegainfer-kv-cache`; host/SSD/RDMA offload bridge in `pegainfer-kv-offload`.

**Build system**: the virtual workspace root has no package build script. `pegainfer-kernels/build.rs` owns CUDA/Triton compilation:
1. Compiles `pegainfer-kernels/csrc/*.cu` with nvcc (auto-detects GPU SM targets)
2. Feature-gated codegen: `qwen35` runs Triton AOT via `pegainfer-kernels/tools/triton/gen_triton_aot.py`; `kimi-k2` adds MLA/MoE/Marlin CUDA; `glm52` adds MLA/MoE/FP8 CUDA plus TileLang sparse-MLA codegen on sm_90a

## EP Free-Running Discipline

Canonical doc: `docs/models/glm52/free-running-dp.md` (K3's gang lane follows it). Invariants — violating any of these is a deadlock design:

- **No rank ever stops or waits.** Every engine loop runs unconditionally at full speed; idle ranks step with padding rows. Any quiet wait (condvar, sleep-poll) inside EP coordination is a bug, and the fleet is never asleep, so never design "wake up" or "pump until X" steps.
- **The per-step collective chain is fixed** — no conditional collectives. Skipping work happens inside kernels via zero-load padding entry, never by host negotiation.
- **The launch count is the global clock** (pairing pins all ranks within ±1 launch). Coordination means agreeing ahead of time on *what step N contains*, never "wait until everyone is ready".
- **Padding rows are protocol surface**: their bytes reach peers, so every dummy-row input must be constructively deterministic.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

15	
16	### 2.1 TTFT 与 TPOT（复习并公式化）
17	
18	u1-l1 引入过这两个指标，这里给出 sim 使用的精确形式：
19	
20	- **TTFT**（Time To First Token，首 token 延迟）：从请求被引擎接受到第一个输出 token 产生的时间。在真实引擎里它由 **prefill 阶段**（一次性读完整个 prompt、填充 KV cache）决定。
21	- **TPOT**（Time Per Output Token，逐 token 耗时）：之后每多生成一个 token 的间隔。在真实引擎里它由 **decode 步长**（每步为一个序列产出一个 token）决定。
22	
23	sim 的 legacy 车道把这两件事抽象成两个可配置的时长：
24	
25	\[ \mathrm{TTFT} = \mathrm{base\_ttft\_ms} + \frac{\mathrm{prompt\_len}}{\mathrm{prefill\_tokens\_per\_ms}} \]
26	
27	\[ \mathrm{TPOT} = \mathrm{tpot\_ms} \]
28	
29	直觉：`base_ttft_ms` 是「无论 prompt 多长都要付的固定启动开销」（kernel 启动、调度等），第二项把 prompt 想象成以 `prefill_tokens_per_ms` 的恒定吞吐被消费——prompt 越长首 token 越晚。TPOT 则完全不依赖序列内容，是一个常数节拍。
30	
31	### 2.2 Rust 的 `Instant` 与 `Duration`
32	
33	- `Instant::now()` 返回单调时钟上的一个时刻（不受系统改时间影响），`Instant + Duration` 得到未来一个时刻，两个 `Instant` 相减得 `Duration`。
34	- `Duration` 内部是「秒 + 纳秒」，构造自 f64 毫秒时要用 `Duration::try_from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0)`；负数或超出表示范围的值会转换失败。
35	
36	### 2.3 f64 的两个陷阱：无穷与 NaN
37	
38	`base_ttft_ms` 等参数是 `f64`。除以 0 会得到 `inf`，`0/0` 会得到 `NaN`，而 `Duration` 无法表示它们。所以你在源码里会看到**两层防线**：`SimulatedEngineConfig::new` 在构造期校验参数，`duration_from_ms` 在换算期再校验一次（见 4.1）。
39	
40	### 2.4 驱动线程模型（谁在调用 step）
41	
42	u1-l3 说过「循环留在前端」。具体地，`spawn_scheduler`（pegainfer-sim 侧调用点在 u1-l3 讲过的 `start_engine_with_partitions` 里）会为每个调度器启动一个 OS 线程，运行前端的 `drive` 循环：**排空提交通道 → 调用一次 `scheduler.step(&mut ledger)` → 发布 metrics → 提交本步账本**，如此往复。`step` 是同步阻塞调用，所以 sim 在 `step` 内部「睡觉」来模拟 GPU 耗时——这是允许的，因为每个分区只有这一个驱动线程，睡觉恰恰就是在「占用虚拟的 GPU」。
43	
44	`RequestLedger`（账本）是前端借给调度器的写入接口：`admit`、`push_tokens`、`finish`、`retire` 等方法只是记账，真正把这一步的 token/终结事件打包发给协议栈的，是驱动循环在 step 结束后的 `commit_step`。

73	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
74	
75	legacy 车道的一切行为都由三个数字驱动：`base_ttft_ms`（固定启动开销）、`prefill_tokens_per_ms`（prefill 吞吐）、`tpot_ms`（decode 节拍）。它们在 u1-l3 讲过的 `SimulatedEngineConfig::new` 里构造期校验（非负、有限、吞吐严格为正），本讲关心的是它们如何被**换算成 `Duration`** 供时间线使用。
76	
77	`duration_from_ms` 是唯一的换算通道，它同时承担防御职责：f64 世界里 `inf`/`NaN`/负数都可能混进来，而 `Duration` 不接受它们——与其在运行期 panic，不如返回 `Err` 让调度器的 `step` 把错误上抛（前端会把它当致命错误处理，见 u4-l4）。

84	    return duration_from_ms(毫秒值)          # 校验 + 换算
85	
86	tpot():
87	    return duration_from_ms(tpot_ms)          # 同一通道
88	
89	duration_from_ms(ms):
90	    1. ensure ms 有限且 >= 0        # 拦 inf / NaN / 负数
91	    2. Duration::try_from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0)  # 拦超出 Duration 表示范围的值
92	    3. 失败时附加上下文返回 Err
93	```

97	| prompt 长度 | TTFT |
98	|------------|------|
99	| 0 token | 5 ms |
100	| 500 token | 5 + 5 = 10 ms |
101	| 2000 token | 5 + 20 = 25 ms |

163	### 4.2 `step_legacy` 全景：admit 循环与 decode 循环
164	
165	#### 4.2.1 概念说明
166	
167	`step_legacy` 是 `Scheduler::step` 在未配置档案时的实现，是 legacy 车道的全部行为。它每次被前端驱动线程调用时做三件事：
168	
169	1. **准入（admit）**：把 `submit` 攒下的队列一次排空——决定这个请求输出什么（`planned_completion` 的交界处，u2-l2 详讲）、记账 `admit`、按 TTFT 预约首 token 时刻；
170	2. **推进（decode）**：遍历所有在跑请求，把「到期了」的各吐一个 token，没到期的保留，吐完的终结；
171	3. **停靠（park）**：如果所有请求的下一个 token 都还没到期，小睡一会再返回（4.4 详讲）。
172	
173	先看分岔点。[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L619-L641](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L619-L641)——trait 实现：`submit` 只是入队（真正的请求来自前端驱动线程排空提交通道后转交过来）；`step` 检查 `self.profiled.is_some()` 决定走哪条车道：
174	
175	```rust
176	fn submit(&mut self, request: QueuedRequest) {
177	    self.queued.push(request);
178	}
179	
180	fn step(&mut self, ledger: &mut RequestLedger) -> Result<()> {
181	    if self.profiled.is_some() {
182	        let mut profiled = self.profiled.take().expect(/* ... */);
183	        let result = profiled.step(&self.config, &mut self.queued, ledger,
184	                                    &mut self.spec_decode, &mut self.prefix_cache);
185	        self.profiled = Some(profiled);
186	        return result;
187	    }
188	    self.step_legacy(ledger)
189	}
190	```
191	
192	（`take()` 再放回去的绕行是为了把 `ProfiledRuntime` 整个借出来、同时还能传 `&self.config` 等字段，避免 `&mut self` 的双重借用。）
193	
194	而调用方循环在 [pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs:L67-L84](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs#L67-L84)：

196	```rust

198	    loop {  // 排空提交通道：register 进账本，转手给 scheduler.submit
199	        match submissions.try_recv() { /* ... */ }
200	    }
201	    let step = scheduler.step(&mut ledger);        // ← step_legacy 在这里被调
202	    let snapshot = scheduler.metrics();
203	    let metrics_changed = metrics.publish(&snapshot);
204	    ledger.commit_step(metrics_changed);           // ← 本步事件此刻才发给协议栈
205	    // step 出错 → fail_all 并退出驱动线程（u4-l4 详讲）
206	}
207	```

209	**关键结论**：新提交的请求只在**两次 step 调用之间**被 drain 进 `self.queued`。这正是 `WAIT_SLICE` 存在的根源（4.4）。

211	#### 4.2.2 核心流程
212	
213	`step_legacy` 的两个循环 + 一次停靠（对应 [L672-L740](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L672-L740)）：
214	
215	```
216	step_legacy(ledger):
217	  # ── 循环 A：准入 ──
218	  for (id, request) in queued.drain(..):
219	      if ledger.is_aborted(id): ledger.retire(id); 跳过     # 客户端已放弃
220	      prefix_cache.note(...)                                 # 假想前缀查找（u4-l2）
221	      (pending, finish_reason) = planned_completion(...)     # 决定输出内容（u2-l2）
222	      ledger.admit(id)
223	      if 请求要 prompt_logprobs: ledger.echo_prompt(...)
224	      if pending 为空: ledger.finish(id, finish_reason); 跳过  # 如 max_tokens=0
225	      running.push(RunningRequest {
226	          next_token_at = Instant::now() + ttft(prompt_len), # ← TTFT 在准入时刻被「烤」进时间线
227	          ...
228	      })
229	
230	  # ── 循环 B：推进 ──
231	  now = Instant::now()
232	  for running in running.drain(..):          # 本步刚准入的也在内！
233	      if ledger.is_aborted: ledger.retire(id); 跳过
234	      if now < next_token_at: 保留; 跳过      # 未到期
235	      token = pending.pop()
236	      if 取不到: ledger.finish(...); 跳过      # 防御分支（见练习 3）
237	      （可选 logprobs 夹具 / 投机解码计数）
238	      ledger.push_tokens(id, [token], ...)
239	      if pending 空了: ledger.finish(id, finish_reason)      # 终结，不再保留
240	      else: next_token_at = Instant::now() + tpot(); 保留    # ← 以「实际吐出时刻」重排节拍
241	
242	  # ── 停靠 ──
243	  park_if_waiting()
244	```
245	
246	一条请求（prompt = `[7, 9, 11]`，`max_tokens = 3`，`base_ttft = 10ms`，`tpot = 50ms`，无脚本）的生命周期时间线（以准入时刻为 t=0）：
247	
248	| 时刻 | 发生的事 | 账本写入 |
249	|------|---------|---------|
250	| t=0（某次 step 的循环 A） | `planned_completion` 生成 3 个待发 token；`next_token_at = t + (10 + 3/100)ms ≈ t+10ms` | `admit` |
251	| t≈10ms（某次 step 的循环 B） | 首 token 到期，弹出并发出；`next_token_at = t'+50ms`（t' 为实际发出时刻） | `push_tokens([token1])` |
252	| t≈60ms | 第二个 token | `push_tokens([token2])` |
253	| t≈110ms | 第三个 token；`pending` 空，同一步内终结 | `push_tokens([token3])` + `finish(Length)` |
254	| 该次 step 返回后 | 前端 `commit_step` 把上面事件打包发给协议栈 | —— |
255	
256	三个值得刻进脑子的结构性质：
257	
258	1. **每个 step 每个请求最多吐一个 token**——循环 B 对每个请求最多 `pop` 一次。这与真实引擎「一个 decode 步为批内每个序列产出一个 token」的 step contract 一致；
259	2. **同一 step 内可完成「准入即吐首 token」**——循环 A 先运行，新请求已进 `self.running`，循环 B 用**新鲜的** `Instant::now()`（L701）比较，TTFT≈0 时立即到期。零成本测试正是靠这一点几步跑完；
260	3. **TPOT 从实际吐出时刻重新起算**（L733 用 `Instant::now()` 而不是循环开头的 `now`）——节拍是「发出到发出」的间隔，不受同批其他请求的数量影响。

354	### 4.3 `RunningRequest` 与 `pending` 反转存储
355	
356	#### 4.3.1 概念说明
357	
358	`RunningRequest` 是「一条已被引擎接受、正在按节拍吐 token 的请求」在调度器里的全部状态。它不保存原始 `Request`（那太大），只保存推进所必需的四样东西：身份、待发 token、下一个到期时刻、终结原因（外加可选的 logprobs 档位）。
359	
360	最有趣的设计是 `pending` 字段：**待发 token 按发出顺序的反方向存放**。`planned_completion` 在生成时是正序的 `Vec<u32>`，返回前做一次 `reverse()`；此后每次发 token 只需 `pop()`——从 Vec 尾部取元素是 O(1)。如果正序存放，就得 `remove(0)`（O(n) 整体搬移）或改用 `VecDeque`。一次 `reverse` 换来整条生命周期的常数弹出，是典型的「构造期付一次成本」。

368	    pending.reverse()                     # ← 反转：栈顶（Vec 尾）= 下一个该发的
369	    return (pending, finish_reason)

449	### 4.4 `park_if_waiting` 与 `WAIT_SLICE` 切片睡眠
450	
451	#### 4.4.1 概念说明
452	
453	循环 B 结束后，若还有请求在跑但下一个 token 都没到期，`step_legacy` 就要回答一个问题：**现在返回吗？**
454	
455	两个极端都不可取：
456	
457	- **立刻返回**：前端驱动循环会马上再调一次 `step`。注意它的空转缓冲有前提——[driver.rs:L94-L103](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs#L94-L103) 只有在 `num_running == 0 && num_waiting == 0` 时才 `spin_loop` 让出发射槽。只要有一条请求在等它的 50ms TPOT，metrics 就报告 running ≥ 1，驱动线程会在两个到期时刻之间**全速空转烧满一个核**。
458	- **睡满整段 TPOT/TTFT**：新请求只在两次 step 之间被 drain（4.2.1 的驱动循环结构）。睡 50ms 甚 至几百 ms 意味着这期间到达的请求全部堵在通道里——它们的实际 TTFT 被人为抬高，客户端 abort 的检测也被拖延。对一个用来「验证前端行为」的 sim，这会系统性扭曲它要测的东西。
459	
460	`WAIT_SLICE = 1ms` 是折中：每步最多睡 1ms，CPU 不空转，同时新请求最多等 1ms 就能被下一次循环准入。源码注释把这两点写得很明白（L40–L43）。
461	
462	#### 4.4.2 核心流程
463	
464	```
465	park_if_waiting():
466	    next = min(所有 running 请求的 next_token_at)   # 没有在跑请求 → None
467	    if next 不存在: return                          # 无事可等，立即返回
468	    now = Instant::now()
469	    if next <= now: return                          # 已有 token 到期，别睡
470	    sleep( min(next - now, WAIT_SLICE) )            # 至多 1ms
471	```
472	
473	配合循环 B 的到期检查，正确的「等到了再发」语义由两者合成保证：park 可能提前 1ms 醒来，但醒后 `step` 被再次调用，循环 B 的 `now < next_token_at` 检查会把未到期请求继续保留——**睡眠只是节能，到期判定只认 `Instant` 比较**。这也意味着 token 间隔的下界是精确的（到期才发），上界受切片粒度影响（最多晚约 1ms + 调度噪声）。

# u2-l1 legacy 定时车道：固定 TTFT/TPOT 的 step 循环

## 1. 本讲目标

学完本讲，你应该能够：

1. **推导时长模型**：解释 `ttft()` 为什么是 `base_ttft_ms + prompt_len / prefill_tokens_per_ms`，`tpot()` 为什么是一个常数，以及这两个公式分别模拟了真实引擎的哪两个阶段（prefill 与 decode）。
2. **解释 `park_if_waiting` 的切片睡眠**：说清楚为什么 `WAIT_SLICE = 1ms` 逐片睡而不是睡满整个 TTFT/TPOT——睡满会冻结准入，完全不睡会烧满一个 CPU 核。
3. **跟踪一条请求的完整事件序列**：从 `submit` 进入队列、`step_legacy` 中被 admit、TTFT 到期发出首 token、按 TPOT 节拍逐 token `push_tokens`，到最后 `Terminal::Finished` 终结。
4. 顺带理解 `RunningRequest` 的 `pending` 字段为什么「反转存储」，以及这条车道如何做到「每个 step 每个请求最多吐一个 token」——这正是与真实引擎一致的 step contract。

本讲承接 u1-l3：那里我们看过 `Scheduler` trait 只有 `submit`/`step`/`metrics` 三个方法，「循环留在前端、行为留在模型线」。本讲就钻进 `SimScheduler` 在**没有配置 `--profile` 档案**时的那条实现路径——legacy 定时车道。

## 2. 前置知识

### 2.1 TTFT 与 TPOT（复习并公式化）

u1-l1 引入过这两个指标，这里给出 sim 使用的精确形式：

- **TTFT**（Time To First Token，首 token 延迟）：从请求被引擎接受到第一个输出 token 产生的时间。在真实引擎里它由 **prefill 阶段**（一次性读完整个 prompt、填充 KV cache）决定。
- **TPOT**（Time Per Output Token，逐 token 耗时）：之后每多生成一个 token 的间隔。在真实引擎里它由 **decode 步长**（每步为一个序列产出一个 token）决定。

sim 的 legacy 车道把这两件事抽象成两个可配置的时长：

\[ \mathrm{TTFT} = \mathrm{base\_ttft\_ms} + \frac{\mathrm{prompt\_len}}{\mathrm{prefill\_tokens\_per\_ms}} \]

\[ \mathrm{TPOT} = \mathrm{tpot\_ms} \]

直觉：`base_ttft_ms` 是「无论 prompt 多长都要付的固定启动开销」（kernel 启动、调度等），第二项把 prompt 想象成以 `prefill_tokens_per_ms` 的恒定吞吐被消费——prompt 越长首 token 越晚。TPOT 则完全不依赖序列内容，是一个常数节拍。

### 2.2 Rust 的 `Instant` 与 `Duration`

- `Instant::now()` 返回单调时钟上的一个时刻（不受系统改时间影响），`Instant + Duration` 得到未来一个时刻，两个 `Instant` 相减得 `Duration`。
- `Duration` 内部是「秒 + 纳秒」，构造自 f64 毫秒时要用 `Duration::try_from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0)`；负数或超出表示范围的值会转换失败。

### 2.3 f64 的两个陷阱：无穷与 NaN

`base_ttft_ms` 等参数是 `f64`。除以 0 会得到 `inf`，`0/0` 会得到 `NaN`，而 `Duration` 无法表示它们。所以你在源码里会看到**两层防线**：`SimulatedEngineConfig::new` 在构造期校验参数，`duration_from_ms` 在换算期再校验一次（见 4.1）。

### 2.4 驱动线程模型（谁在调用 step）

u1-l3 说过「循环留在前端」。具体地，`spawn_scheduler`（pegainfer-sim 侧调用点在 u1-l3 讲过的 `start_engine_with_partitions` 里）会为每个调度器启动一个 OS 线程，运行前端的 `drive` 循环：**排空提交通道 → 调用一次 `scheduler.step(&mut ledger)` → 发布 metrics → 提交本步账本**，如此往复。`step` 是同步阻塞调用，所以 sim 在 `step` 内部「睡觉」来模拟 GPU 耗时——这是允许的，因为每个分区只有这一个驱动线程，睡觉恰恰就是在「占用虚拟的 GPU」。

`RequestLedger`（账本）是前端借给调度器的写入接口：`admit`、`push_tokens`、`finish`、`retire` 等方法只是记账，真正把这一步的 token/终结事件打包发给协议栈的，是驱动循环在 step 结束后的 `commit_step`。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

本讲的核心源码只有一个文件，但会在两处「越界」看一眼前端：

| 文件 | 作用 | 本讲关注的区域 |
|------|------|----------------|
| `pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs` | sim 引擎全部核心逻辑 | `WAIT_SLICE` 常量、`ttft`/`tpot`/`duration_from_ms`、`RunningRequest`、`step_legacy`、`park_if_waiting`、`collect_completion` 测试辅助 |
| `pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs`（只读参考） | 前端驱动循环与 `Scheduler` trait 定义 | `drive` 主循环——确认「谁在调 step、新请求何时被 drain」 |

`src/lib.rs` 内部区域速查（行号基于当前 HEAD）：

| 行号 | 内容 |
|------|------|
| L40–L43 | `WAIT_SLICE` 常量及其设计理由注释 |
| L148–L154 | `ttft()` / `tpot()` |
| L261–L277 | `SimScheduler` 与 `RunningRequest` 结构体 |
| L607–L616 | `park_if_waiting` |
| L619–L641 | `Scheduler` trait 实现（车道分岔点） |
| L672–L740 | `step_legacy`（本讲主角） |
| L744–L784 | `planned_completion` / `fake_token_id`（u2-l2 深入，本讲只看交界处） |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 时长模型：`ttft` / `tpot` / `duration_from_ms`

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

legacy 车道的一切行为都由三个数字驱动：`base_ttft_ms`（固定启动开销）、`prefill_tokens_per_ms`（prefill 吞吐）、`tpot_ms`（decode 节拍）。它们在 u1-l3 讲过的 `SimulatedEngineConfig::new` 里构造期校验（非负、有限、吞吐严格为正），本讲关心的是它们如何被**换算成 `Duration`** 供时间线使用。

`duration_from_ms` 是唯一的换算通道，它同时承担防御职责：f64 世界里 `inf`/`NaN`/负数都可能混进来，而 `Duration` 不接受它们——与其在运行期 panic，不如返回 `Err` 让调度器的 `step` 把错误上抛（前端会把它当致命错误处理，见 u4-l4）。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```
ttft(prompt_len):
    毫秒值 = base_ttft_ms + prompt_len / prefill_tokens_per_ms
    return duration_from_ms(毫秒值)          # 校验 + 换算

tpot():
    return duration_from_ms(tpot_ms)          # 同一通道

duration_from_ms(ms):
    1. ensure ms 有限且 >= 0        # 拦 inf / NaN / 负数
    2. Duration::try_from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0)  # 拦超出 Duration 表示范围的值
    3. 失败时附加上下文返回 Err
```

速算表（默认配置 `base=5.0`、`100.0 tok/ms`，见 `Default` 实现）：

| prompt 长度 | TTFT |
|------------|------|
| 0 token | 5 ms |
| 500 token | 5 + 5 = 10 ms |
| 2000 token | 5 + 20 = 25 ms |

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L148-L154](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L148-L154)——两个时长查询方法，都是私有方法，只被 legacy 车道使用：

```rust
fn ttft(&self, prompt_tokens: usize) -> Result<Duration> {
    duration_from_ms(self.base_ttft_ms + prompt_tokens as f64 / self.prefill_tokens_per_ms)
}

fn tpot(&self) -> Result<Duration> {
    duration_from_ms(self.tpot_ms)
}
```

`ttft` 是公式的直接翻译：固定项 + prompt 长度除以吞吐。注意它返回 `Result`——派生值（和、商）可能失去原始参数的良构性，所以换算函数有权拒绝。

[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L786-L793](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L786-L793)——唯一的 f64→Duration 通道：

```rust
fn duration_from_ms(ms: f64) -> Result<Duration> {
    ensure!(
        ms.is_finite() && ms >= 0.0,
        "timing value must be finite and non-negative"
    );
    Duration::try_from_secs_f64(ms / 1000.0)
        .context("timing value is not representable as a Duration")
}
```

两道闸门：`ensure!` 拦非有限值和负数；`try_from_secs_f64` 拦「有限但大到 `Duration` 装不下」的值。两者都变成带上下文的 `anyhow` 错误。

[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L157-L170](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L157-L170)——`Default` 给出的缺省定时：`base_ttft_ms: 5.0`、`prefill_tokens_per_ms: 100.0`、`tpot_ms: 12.0`。CLI 不传定时参数时（u1-l2 讲过的 `DEFAULT_*` 常量）最终落点与这组值对应。

[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L1015-L1022](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L1015-L1022)——构造期防线的测试：`config_rejects_invalid_timing_values` 用六个断言逐一覆盖负 base、零吞吐、负 TPOT、NaN、正无穷 base、正无穷 TPOT。**注意零 TPOT 不在其中**——`tpot_ms = 0.0` 是合法配置，它把 decode 节拍归零，是「零成本」测试（如 L1025 的测试）能瞬间跑完的前提。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

1. **实践目标**：把 4.1.3 的两道防线和测试一一对应起来。
2. **操作步骤**：在工作区根目录运行

3. **需要观察的现象**：测试通过；`--nocapture` 下无额外输出（该测试只有断言）。
4. **预期结果**：通过后，逐行核对六个 `assert!(...is_err())` 分别对应 `SimulatedEngineConfig::new` 里哪个 `ensure!`（负/非有限 base、非正吞吐、负/非有限 TPOT——L75–L86 区间的三段校验各出现两次）。
5. 本实践为已存在测试的运行与阅读，可直接复现。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：默认配置下，2000 token 的 prompt 首 token 多久之后出现？
**答案**：\( 5 + 2000/100 = 25 \) ms。

**练习 2**：为什么 `prefill_tokens_per_ms` 要求**严格为正**，而 `tpot_ms` 只要求非负？
**答案**：吞吐出现在**分母**上，为 0 时 `prompt_len / 0` 会产生 `inf`（或空 prompt 时 `0/0 = NaN`），虽然 `duration_from_ms` 也会在换算期拦住它，但构造期就拒绝能把错误提前到配置面（fail-fast，与 u1-l2 讲过的互斥校验同一哲学）；TPOT 为 0 则是良构的「零成本 decode」，测试大量依赖它。

**练习 3**：`new` 已经校验过参数，`duration_from_ms` 为什么还要再校验一遍？
**答案**：防御纵深。`new` 校验的是**原始参数**；`ttft()` 换算的是**派生值**（和、商），且 `Duration::try_from_secs_f64` 对「有限但超大」的值同样会失败——第二道闸门覆盖的是第一道管不到的输入。

### 4.2 `step_legacy` 全景：admit 循环与 decode 循环

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`step_legacy` 是 `Scheduler::step` 在未配置档案时的实现，是 legacy 车道的全部行为。它每次被前端驱动线程调用时做三件事：

1. **准入（admit）**：把 `submit` 攒下的队列一次排空——决定这个请求输出什么（`planned_completion` 的交界处，u2-l2 详讲）、记账 `admit`、按 TTFT 预约首 token 时刻；
2. **推进（decode）**：遍历所有在跑请求，把「到期了」的各吐一个 token，没到期的保留，吐完的终结；
3. **停靠（park）**：如果所有请求的下一个 token 都还没到期，小睡一会再返回（4.4 详讲）。

先看分岔点。[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L619-L641](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L619-L641)——trait 实现：`submit` 只是入队（真正的请求来自前端驱动线程排空提交通道后转交过来）；`step` 检查 `self.profiled.is_some()` 决定走哪条车道：

```rust
fn submit(&mut self, request: QueuedRequest) {
    self.queued.push(request);
}

fn step(&mut self, ledger: &mut RequestLedger) -> Result<()> {
    if self.profiled.is_some() {
        let mut profiled = self.profiled.take().expect(/* ... */);
        let result = profiled.step(&self.config, &mut self.queued, ledger,
                                    &mut self.spec_decode, &mut self.prefix_cache);
        self.profiled = Some(profiled);
        return result;
    }
    self.step_legacy(ledger)
}
```

（`take()` 再放回去的绕行是为了把 `ProfiledRuntime` 整个借出来、同时还能传 `&self.config` 等字段，避免 `&mut self` 的双重借用。）

而调用方循环在 [pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs:L67-L84](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs#L67-L84)：

```rust
loop {
    loop {  // 排空提交通道：register 进账本，转手给 scheduler.submit
        match submissions.try_recv() { /* ... */ }
    }
    let step = scheduler.step(&mut ledger);        // ← step_legacy 在这里被调
    let snapshot = scheduler.metrics();
    let metrics_changed = metrics.publish(&snapshot);
    ledger.commit_step(metrics_changed);           // ← 本步事件此刻才发给协议栈
    // step 出错 → fail_all 并退出驱动线程（u4-l4 详讲）
}
```

**关键结论**：新提交的请求只在**两次 step 调用之间**被 drain 进 `self.queued`。这正是 `WAIT_SLICE` 存在的根源（4.4）。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

`step_legacy` 的两个循环 + 一次停靠（对应 [L672-L740](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L672-L740)）：

```
step_legacy(ledger):
  # ── 循环 A：准入 ──
  for (id, request) in queued.drain(..):
      if ledger.is_aborted(id): ledger.retire(id); 跳过     # 客户端已放弃
      prefix_cache.note(...)                                 # 假想前缀查找（u4-l2）
      (pending, finish_reason) = planned_completion(...)     # 决定输出内容（u2-l2）
      ledger.admit(id)
      if 请求要 prompt_logprobs: ledger.echo_prompt(...)
      if pending 为空: ledger.finish(id, finish_reason); 跳过  # 如 max_tokens=0
      running.push(RunningRequest {
          next_token_at = Instant::now() + ttft(prompt_len), # ← TTFT 在准入时刻被「烤」进时间线
          ...
      })

  # ── 循环 B：推进 ──
  now = Instant::now()
  for running in running.drain(..):          # 本步刚准入的也在内！
      if ledger.is_aborted: ledger.retire(id); 跳过
      if now < next_token_at: 保留; 跳过      # 未到期
      token = pending.pop()
      if 取不到: ledger.finish(...); 跳过      # 防御分支（见练习 3）
      （可选 logprobs 夹具 / 投机解码计数）
      ledger.push_tokens(id, [token], ...)
      if pending 空了: ledger.finish(id, finish_reason)      # 终结，不再保留
      else: next_token_at = Instant::now() + tpot(); 保留    # ← 以「实际吐出时刻」重排节拍

  # ── 停靠 ──
  park_if_waiting()
```

一条请求（prompt = `[7, 9, 11]`，`max_tokens = 3`，`base_ttft = 10ms`，`tpot = 50ms`，无脚本）的生命周期时间线（以准入时刻为 t=0）：

| 时刻 | 发生的事 | 账本写入 |
|------|---------|---------|
| t=0（某次 step 的循环 A） | `planned_completion` 生成 3 个待发 token；`next_token_at = t + (10 + 3/100)ms ≈ t+10ms` | `admit` |
| t≈10ms（某次 step 的循环 B） | 首 token 到期，弹出并发出；`next_token_at = t'+50ms`（t' 为实际发出时刻） | `push_tokens([token1])` |
| t≈60ms | 第二个 token | `push_tokens([token2])` |
| t≈110ms | 第三个 token；`pending` 空，同一步内终结 | `push_tokens([token3])` + `finish(Length)` |
| 该次 step 返回后 | 前端 `commit_step` 把上面事件打包发给协议栈 | —— |

三个值得刻进脑子的结构性质：

1. **每个 step 每个请求最多吐一个 token**——循环 B 对每个请求最多 `pop` 一次。这与真实引擎「一个 decode 步为批内每个序列产出一个 token」的 step contract 一致；
2. **同一 step 内可完成「准入即吐首 token」**——循环 A 先运行，新请求已进 `self.running`，循环 B 用**新鲜的** `Instant::now()`（L701）比较，TTFT≈0 时立即到期。零成本测试正是靠这一点几步跑完；
3. **TPOT 从实际吐出时刻重新起算**（L733 用 `Instant::now()` 而不是循环开头的 `now`）——节拍是「发出到发出」的间隔，不受同批其他请求的数量影响。

```rust

    if ledger.is_aborted(id) {
        ledger.retire(id);
        continue;
    }
    // The pretend lookup happens exactly where a real engine would do
    // it: once, on admission.
    self.prefix_cache.note(self.config.prefix_cache, &request);
    let prompt_len = request.prompt_tokens.len();
    let (pending, finish_reason) =
        planned_completion(&self.config, &request.prompt_tokens, request.max_tokens);
    ledger.admit(id);
    // ... prompt_logprobs 回显（略） ...

        continue;

        id,
        pending,
        next_token_at: Instant::now() + self.config.ttft(prompt_len)?,
        // ...
    });

```

两个细节：`pending` 为空（例如 `max_tokens = 0`）的请求**准入即终结**，从不进入 `running`；`next_token_at` 在准入时刻就算好——TTFT 是「预约制」，之后每步只是对表。

[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L701-L737](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L701-L737)——推进循环。`drain` + 重建 `still_running` 的写法让「移出」天然发生：终结/中止的请求不 push 回去，其余保留：

```rust

let mut still_running = Vec::new();
for mut running in self.running.drain(..) {
    if ledger.is_aborted(running.id) {
        ledger.retire(running.id);
        continue;
    }
    if now < running.next_token_at {
        still_running.push(running);
        continue;
    }
    let Some(token) = running.pending.pop() else {
        ledger.finish(running.id, running.finish_reason);
        continue;
    };
    // ... logprobs 夹具与投机解码计数（略） ...
    ledger.push_tokens(running.id, &[token], &logprobs);
    if running.pending.is_empty() {
        ledger.finish(running.id, running.finish_reason);
    } else {
        running.next_token_at = Instant::now() + self.config.tpot()?;
        still_running.push(running);
    }
}

```

注意 `let Some(token) = ... else { finish }` 这个分支实际**不可达**（练习 3 会问为什么），它是对「空 pending 的请求不该留在 running」这一不变量的防御性守卫。中止检查在两个循环里各出现一次——legacy 车道的取消语义就这两行 `retire`，深度对比留给 u2-l5。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：`max_tokens = 0` 的请求在 legacy 车道会发生什么？
**答案**：`planned_completion` 的 `emit_count` 为 0，返回空 `pending`；准入循环里命中 `if pending.is_empty()` 分支（L688–L691），**同一步内** `admit` 后立即 `finish`，从不进入 `running`，TTFT/TPOT 与它无关。

**练习 2**：同一个 `step` 调用里，刚 admit 的请求可能立刻发出首 token 吗？
**答案**：可能。循环 A 先于循环 B 执行，新请求已 push 进 `self.running`；循环 B 开头重新取 `Instant::now()`（L701），只要 TTFT 换算出的时长小于循环 A 到 B 之间流逝的时间（比如 TTFT=0.03ms），首 token 就在**准入的同一个 step**里发出。零成本测试依赖这一点快速收敛。

**练习 3**：循环 B 里 `let Some(token) = running.pending.pop() else { finish }` 什么时候触发？
**答案**：实际不可达，是防御性守卫。不变量是「pending 为空的请求不留在 running」：准入时空 pending 会立即 finish（L688）；发出最后一个 token 的同一步也会 finish（L730–L731）。如果未来改动破坏了这个不变量，这个分支会把请求体面终结而不是 panic 或静默卡死。

### 4.3 `RunningRequest` 与 `pending` 反转存储

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

`RunningRequest` 是「一条已被引擎接受、正在按节拍吐 token 的请求」在调度器里的全部状态。它不保存原始 `Request`（那太大），只保存推进所必需的四样东西：身份、待发 token、下一个到期时刻、终结原因（外加可选的 logprobs 档位）。

最有趣的设计是 `pending` 字段：**待发 token 按发出顺序的反方向存放**。`planned_completion` 在生成时是正序的 `Vec<u32>`，返回前做一次 `reverse()`；此后每次发 token 只需 `pop()`——从 Vec 尾部取元素是 O(1)。如果正序存放，就得 `remove(0)`（O(n) 整体搬移）或改用 `VecDeque`。一次 `reverse` 换来整条生命周期的常数弹出，是典型的「构造期付一次成本」。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

```
planned_completion:                       # u2-l2 详讲，这里只看交界
    emit_count = max_tokens（无脚本时）
    pending = [第0个, 第1个, ..., 第emit_count-1个]   # 正序
    pending.reverse()                     # ← 反转：栈顶（Vec 尾）= 下一个该发的
    return (pending, finish_reason)

step_legacy 循环 B:
    token = running.pending.pop()         # O(1)，取到的正是「下一个」token
```

无脚本时第 i 个 token 由 `fake_token_id(prompt, i, fallback)` 决定：prompt 非空时循环取 `prompt[i % len]`，空 prompt 用 fallback（[L779-L784](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L779-L784)）。所以无脚本模式下「引擎的输出」就是把 prompt 自己循环复读——这足以驱动前端全链路，又完全可预测。

[pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs:L744-L769](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-sim/src/lib.rs#L744-L769) 的函数把「发什么」与「何时发」解耦：`planned_completion` 只管内容与 `FinishReason`（脚本重放完 → `Stop`；被 `max_tokens` 截断或无脚本 → `Length`），`step_legacy` 只管时间线。这个解耦让 u2-l2 可以单独深讲内容、本讲单独深讲时间。

### 4.4 `park_if_waiting` 与 `WAIT_SLICE` 切片睡眠

#### 4.4.1 概念说明

循环 B 结束后，若还有请求在跑但下一个 token 都没到期，`step_legacy` 就要回答一个问题：**现在返回吗？**

两个极端都不可取：

- **立刻返回**：前端驱动循环会马上再调一次 `step`。注意它的空转缓冲有前提——[driver.rs:L94-L103](https://github.com/openinfer-project/openinfer/blob/af9e40e12108141bb18f93188c82d2583df18509/pegainfer-frontend/src/engine/driver.rs#L94-L103) 只有在 `num_running == 0 && num_waiting == 0` 时才 `spin_loop` 让出发射槽。只要有一条请求在等它的 50ms TPOT，metrics 就报告 running ≥ 1，驱动线程会在两个到期时刻之间**全速空转烧满一个核**。
